answer: An agent economy can require every trading identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether it tracks sparrow populations, schedules harbor traffic, or maps glacier retreat. Creating 10,000 fake identities then ties up $1 million for a month. Splitting into more accounts creates no free capacity: each extra identity requires fresh collateral, making a sybil swarm costly through both capital requirements and lost access to that money.
